source_data.prob_desc_description: Mahmoud and Ehab play a game called the even-odd game. Ehab chooses his favorite integer n and then they take turns, starting from Mahmoud. In each player's turn, he has to choose an integer a and subtract it from n such that:  1 ≤ a ≤ n.  If it's Mahmoud's turn, a has to be even, but if it's Ehab's turn, a has to be odd. If the current player can't choose any number satisfying the conditions, he loses. Can you determine the winner if they both play optimally?
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Output "Mahmoud" (without quotes) if Mahmoud wins and "Ehab" (without quotes) otherwise.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The only line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 109), the number at the beginning of the game.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first sample, Mahmoud can't choose any integer a initially because there is no positive even integer less than or equal to 1 so Ehab wins.In the second sample, Mahmoud has to choose a = 2 and subtract it from n. It's Ehab's turn and n = 0. There is no positive odd integer less than or equal to 0 so Mahmoud wins.
